hook.line: A witness in a crowded assembly rarely saw everything. Spanish has a neat way to say you caught something, or just missed it, without sounding like you simply refuse to look.
hook.es: No alcancé a ver quién era.
hook.en: I didn't manage to see who it was.

examples.es: No alcancé a ver quién era.
examples.en: I didn't manage to see who it was.

examples.es: Alcancé a oír lo que dijo.
examples.en: I managed to hear what he said.

examples.es: Desde aquí no distingo si es él.
examples.en: From here I can't make out whether it's him.

examples.es: No alcanzo a leer el letrero.
examples.en: I can't quite read the sign.

examples.es: La torre se ve de lejos.
examples.en: The tower can be seen from far away.

examples.es: Desde la ventana se ve la plaza.
examples.en: From the window you can see the plaza.

rule:
*Alcanzar a* + ver, oír, leer or entender means you just managed to catch it, or just didn't: *Alcancé a oír* (I caught it), *No alcancé a ver* (I couldn't make it out). The *a* is part of the phrase.

*Distinguir* is to tell something apart: *No distingo si es él.*

For what can be seen or heard from a place, Spanish uses *se*: *La torre se ve de lejos.* *Se oye la música.*
smallPrint: Teachers call *alcanzar a* a verb of attainment: it is about your eyes or ears reaching the thing, not about deciding to look.

I saw who it was.

From here I don't know him.

yourTurn.prompt: I didn't manage to read the whole minutes. Choose *alcancé* or *alcanzó*: No ___ a leer el acta completa.
yourTurn.answer: No alcancé a leer el acta completa.
accept: No alcancé a leer el acta completa
yourTurn.why: It is about "I", so the ending is *-é*: *alcancé*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I managed to hear what he said.
yourTurn.answer: Alcancé a oír lo que dijo.
accept: Alcancé a oír lo que dijo
Alcancé a escuchar lo que dijo.
yourTurn.why: *Alcancé a* + infinitive: you just caught it.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: With so many people, I can't make out who is speaking.
yourTurn.answer: Con tanta gente no alcanzo a distinguir quién habla.
accept: Con tanta gente no alcanzo a distinguir quién habla
Con tanta gente no distingo quién habla.
yourTurn.why: *No alcanzo a distinguir* says you can't quite tell them apart.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: From the window you can see the plaza.
yourTurn.answer: Desde la ventana se ve la plaza.
accept: Desde la ventana se ve la plaza
Se ve la plaza desde la ventana.
yourTurn.why: *Se ve* is the everyday way to say what can be seen from somewhere.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you manage to see who it was?
Make it negative: Alcancé a entender qué pasó.
yourTurn.answer: No alcancé a entender qué pasó.
accept: No alcancé a entender qué pasó
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front and it means you didn't catch it.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about her: Alcancé a ver quién era.
accept: Ella alcanzó a ver quién era.

pitfalls.right: No alcancé a ver quién era.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The small *a* is part of *alcanzar a*, and English has nothing like it.

pitfalls.wrong: La torre es vista de lejos.
pitfalls.right: La torre se ve de lejos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "is seen"; Spanish says *se ve*.

pitfalls.wrong: Desde aquí no distingo que es él.
pitfalls.right: Desde aquí no distingo si es él.

personal: Think of a crowded place you know. Say one thing you can't quite make out there, and one thing that can be seen from far away: *No alcanzo a…*, *Se ve…*
